title: Progress of area coverage under Kharif crops as on 14.08.2026
body_text:
Area:  In lakh hectare S. No. Crop Normal Area (2020-21 to 2024-25) Final Area Coverage 2025 Area Sown 2026 2025 Increase(+)/ Decrease(-) over 2025 1 Rice 412.00 446.70 379.07 393.44 -14.37 2 Pulses 123.64 118.97 108.14 108.49 -0.35 a Arhar 44.32 44.60 40.31 42.01 -1.69 b Urdbean 29.60 21.26 23.52 20.79 2.73 c Moongbean 35.48 37.45 32.05 33.42 -1.37 d Kulthi 1.48 0.19 0.18 0.01 e Mothbean 9.69 8.92 8.69 0.23 f Other pulses 3.07 15.66 3.14 3.40 -0.27 3 Shri Anna cum Coarse cereals 182.63 192.12 172.96 177.13 -4.17 a Jowar 14.44 12.10 13.30 12.61 0.69 b Bajra** 70.94 63.80 63.98 63.29 0.69 c Ragi 12.01 13.46 3.46 5.26 -1.80 d Small millets 4.47 4.15 3.83 3.92 -0.09 e Maize 80.77 98.61 88.39 92.06 -3.67 4 Oilseeds 200.08 196.38 184.46 185.36 -0.89 a Groundnut 46.79 50.29 48.03 47.01 1.02 b Soybean 128.71 123.86 120.84 122.61 -1.76 c Sunflower 1.20 0.88 1.06 0.61 0.46 d Sesamum 12.88 9.63 10.35 8.73 1.63 e Niger 1.01 0.83 0.24 0.16 0.08 f Castor 9.49 10.89 3.83 6.19 -2.35 g Other Oilseeds 0.00 0.10 0.06 0.04 5 Sugarcane 54.20 58.84 58.31 58.62 -0.31 6 Jute & Mesta 6.40 6.06 6.34 6.23 0.11 7 Cotton 125.51 115.20 107.30 108.26 -0.96 Total 1104.46 1134.27 1016.57 1037.52 -20.95 Rice : About 379.07 lakh ha area coverage under rice has been reported as compared to 393.44 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year, showing a decrease of 14.37 lakh ha. The major decrease in area has been reported in the states of Karnataka (2.86 lakh ha), Jharkhand (2.26 lakh ha), Maharashtra (2.25 lakh ha), Odisha (2.09 lakh ha), Madhya Pradesh (1.64 lakh ha), Telangana (1.49 lakh ha), Tamil Nadu (1.17 lakh ha), Andhra Pradesh (1.14 lakh ha), Gujarat (0.83 lakh ha), West Bengal (0.87 lakh ha), Uttar Pradesh (0.58 lakh ha)  and Bihar (0.52 lakh ha).  Higher area coverage has been reported in Assam (3.93 lakh ha), Uttarakhand (0.35 lakh ha), etc. Pulses: About 108.14 lakh ha area coverage under pulses has been reported as compared to 108.49 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year, showing a decrease of 0.35 lakh ha. The major decrease in area has been reported in the states of Karnataka (4.16 lakh ha), Maharashtra (2.70 lakh ha), Odisha (0.64 lakh ha), Tamil Nadu (0.13 lakh ha) and Bihar (0.14 lakh ha). Higher area coverage has been reported in the states of Uttar Pradesh (4.25 lakh ha), Rajasthan (0.93 lakh ha), Chhattisgarh (0.40 lakh ha), Andhra Pradesh (0.35 lakh ha), Telangana (0.34 lakh ha), Madhya Pradesh (0.14 lakh ha), etc. Shree Anna & Coarse Cereals: About 172.96 lakh ha area coverage under Shree Anna & Coarse Cereals has been reported as compared to 177.13 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year, showing a decrease of 4.17 lakh ha. The major decrease in area has been reported in the states of Karnataka (7.00 lakh ha), Maharashtra (2.46 lakh ha), Haryana (0.59 lakh ha), Tamil Nadu (0.30 lakh ha), Telangana (0.31 lakh ha), Andhra Pradesh (0.36 lakh ha), Jammu & Kashmir (0.19 lakh ha) and Gujarat (0.09 lakh ha). Higher area coverage has been reported in the states of Rajasthan (2.15 lakh ha), Chhattisgarh (1.53 lakh ha), Madhya Pradesh (0.92 lakh ha), Odisha (0.68 lakh ha), Uttar Pradesh (0.62 lakh ha), Bihar (0.59 lakh ha), Uttarakhand (0.42 lakh ha), Jharkhand (0.20 lakh ha) and Himachal Pradesh (0.09 lakh ha), etc. Oilseeds: About 184.46 lakh ha area coverage under oilseeds has been reported as compared to 185.36 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year, showing a decrease of 0.89 lakh ha. The major decrease in area has been reported in the states of Rajasthan (3.40 lakh ha), Maharashtra (0.56 lakh ha), Gujarat (1.00 lakh ha), Karnataka (0.44 lakh ha), Tamil Nadu (0.13 lakh ha), Odisha (0.16 lakh ha), etc.The higher area coverage has been reported in the states of Uttar Pradesh (3.89 lakh ha), Madhya Pradesh (0.68 lakh ha), Assam (0.10 lakh ha), etc. Sugarcane: About 58.31 lakh ha area coverage under sugarcane has been reported as compared to 58.62 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year, showing a decrease of 0.31 lakh ha. The major decrease in area has been reported in the states of Uttarakhand (0.20 lakh ha), Maharashtra (0.14 lakh ha), Punjab (0.14 lakh ha), Madhya Pradesh (0.12 lakh ha), etc. Higher area coverage has been reported in the states of Uttar Pradesh (0.36 lakh ha), Haryana (0.11 lakh ha), etc. Jute & Mesta: About 6.34 lakh ha area coverage under Jute & Mesta has been reported compared to 6.23 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. Thus increase by 0.11 lakh ha majourly in Bihar (0.11 lakh ha). Cotton: About 107.30 lakh ha area coverage under cotton has been reported as compared to 108.26 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year, showing a decrease of 0.96 lakh ha. The major decrease in area has been reported in the states of Rajasthan (1.09 lakh ha), Haryana (0.90 lakh ha), Punjab (0.43 lakh ha), Maharashtra (0.38 lakh ha), Karnataka (0.10 lakh ha), Uttar Pradesh (0.05 lakh ha) and Odisha (0.01 lakh ha). Higher area coverage has been reported mainly in the states of Telangana (1.25 lakh ha), Gujarat (0.64 lakh ha), Madhya Pradesh (0.11 lakh ha) and Andhra Pradesh (0.02 lakh ha).

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare released data on Kharif crop area coverage as on 14 August 2026, showing total sown area of 1016.57 lakh hectares, a decrease of 20.95 lakh hectares compared to the same period last year (1037.52 lakh ha). Rice, pulses, coarse cereals, oilseeds, sugarcane and cotton all recorded marginal to significant declines in area, while jute & mesta saw a slight increase. State-wise variations show declines concentrated in Karnataka, Maharashtra, and Odisha, with gains in Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Assam for various crops.
enrichment.context:
This is a routine periodic bulletin issued by the Ministry of Agriculture during the Kharif sowing season, tracking real-time progress of crop area coverage against normal averages (2020-21 to 2024-25) and the previous year's figures. Such data helps monitor monsoon performance, cropping pattern shifts, and potential production trends, feeding into subsequent estimates like the First Advance Estimates of foodgrain production. Kharif crops—rice, pulses, coarse cereals (Shree Anna), oilseeds, cotton, sugarcane, and jute—are sown with the onset of the southwest monsoon (June-July) and harvested around October, making their area coverage sensitive to rainfall distribution.

These bulletins are released multiple times during the sowing season and are largely administrative/statistical in nature, useful for tracking agricultural trends but not typically containing new policy announcements. The consistent decline in rice area (14.37 lakh ha) alongside gains in coarse cereals like jowar and bajra could reflect a mix of rainfall patterns and diversification encouraged under the Shree Anna (millets) promotion initiative launched following the International Year of Millets (2023).
